note: Multi-step journeys captured step by step. Each step has a viewport image (what a person met) and a full-page image (the record). Companion to screens.json, which holds single screens.

flows.name: Register to vote — the full application, up to the summary
flows.source: GOV.UK / Register to vote (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government)
flows.licence_note: Crown copyright. All content available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, as stated in the service footer. Captured for closed-module teaching use; not republished.
flows.walk_note: Walked to 'Check your answers before sending your application' and STOPPED. 'Accept and send' was never pressed — the page itself warns that knowingly providing false information in a registration application is an offence carrying an unlimited fine and up to 51 weeks' imprisonment. No application was submitted and no record was created.
flows.test_data: Name Joe Doe · DOB 1 Jan 1990 · email joe.doe@example.com (IANA-reserved documentation domain, unroutable) · phone 020 7946 0018 (Ofcom drama-reserved range) · National Insurance number NOT invented — the 'I cannot provide' path was used instead.
flows.point_of_interest: Postcode E9 7HQ, the westernmost point of Victoria Park, east London (lon -0.05281, lat 51.53508, Regent's Canal towpath corner).
flows.why: A long, linear government form with a summary-and-change pattern at the end. One question per page, an exception path on the NI number, a consent decision on the open register, and a session-timeout warning that fires mid-flow.
flows.annotation_note: reading_order[] and devices_used[] are null on every step and must stay null until a person fills them — same rule as screens.json.

flows.name: Find a GP — postcode to provider to how to register
flows.licence_note: © NHS England. Captured for closed-module teaching use; not republished. Check NHS website terms before any onward use.
flows.walk_note: Read-only throughout. No account, no login, no form submitted beyond a postcode search.
flows.test_data: Postcode E9 7HQ only. No personal data entered.
flows.point_of_interest: Same postcode as sd-flow-001 — the westernmost point of Victoria Park, east London.
flows.why: A search-to-result-to-detail journey. Carries a live status banner ('This GP surgery is currently closed'), an availability filter, an 'Accepting new patients' state chip, and a results list long enough that a full-page capture runs to 54,000 pixels — which is itself the lesson about capture method.
flows.annotation_note: reading_order[] and devices_used[] are null on every step and must stay null until a person fills them — same rule as screens.json.

flows.name: News front page — front page to lead story
flows.licence_note: © BBC. All rights reserved. Captured for closed-module teaching use under fair dealing for illustration for instruction; NOT republished and not to be placed on a public webroot.
flows.walk_note: Read-only. No account, no login, nothing submitted. Front page captured after a full scroll pass so lazy-loaded images resolved — an unscrolled capture leaves the lead image grey and destroys the hierarchy the page is being read for.
flows.why: The purest hierarchy exercise available: a front page exists to answer 'what is the most important thing today' in one glance. The lead is set by scale, a display serif against the sans body, and top-left position. Note also that the front page carries no h1 — a checkable accessibility finding, not an opinion.
flows.annotation_note: reading_order[] and devices_used[] stay null until a person fills them.

flows.name: Retail checkout — product page (INCOMPLETE)
flows.licence_note: © Screwfix Direct Ltd. Captured for closed-module teaching use under fair dealing for illustration for instruction; NOT republished.
flows.walk_note: INCOMPLETE. Nothing was added to a basket and no checkout was reached. Of seven UK retailers tested for reachability, six refused an automated request outright (403 or no response); Screwfix answered, but its Collect/Deliver fulfilment control would not accept a scripted click even with the consent overlay dismissed. The product page and the TrustArc consent modal were captured; the basket and checkout screens were not. Finishing this flow needs a hand-driven pass, not a longer script.
flows.test_data: None. No basket, no personal data, no payment details — payment screens are out of scope for this corpus in any case.
flows.why: Kept despite being incomplete because two of its screens already earn their place: a product page that puts a Collect/Deliver decision above the price, and a consent modal that dims the entire page and gives Accept and Reject equal visual weight — which is rarer, and better, than most.
